title: Vision Transport Layer
summary: Moves camera frames from physical cameras into the Cognitive OS as rich Frame objects, routed only through the Camera Manager. Transport only: no reasoning, no observations, no World Model writes.
responsibility: Transport image frames from cameras into the COS. Nothing more.
pipeline_position: Reality -> Camera -> [Vision Transport Layer] -> Frame Objects -> (Vision Processing -> Observation Builder -> ...) [later parts]

components.Frame: rich frame object (replaces raw numpy arrays)
components.CameraAdapter: pull (webcam/RTSP/array) or PushAdapter (browser/ESP32) - add a camera = add an adapter
components.FrameQueue: thread-safe bounded queue, overflow policy (drop_oldest|drop_newest|block), back-pressure, metrics
components.FrameDecoder: cv2 -> Pillow -> none; runs off the socket thread
components.CameraRegistry: permanent key->id mapping (in-memory or SQLite data/vision.db)
components.VisionTransportServer: productionized Flask+SocketIO ingress (lazy import; legacy 'frame' protocol preserved)

configuration.deps: core: numpy; optional: cv2/Pillow (decode), flask+flask-socketio (server), pyngrok (tunnel)

public_api: connect_browser(token, label) / add_webcam(source) / add_rtsp(url) / add_array_camera(key, frames) / register(adapter)
cameras() / dashboard() / health() / metrics() / manifest() / attach(runtime) / start() / stop()
invariants: no subsystem accesses transport sockets directly (only the Camera Manager)
downstream consumes Frame objects, never raw arrays
cameras referenced only by permanent CAMERA_id (never ip/socket/session)
transport performs zero cognition (cannot corrupt the World Model)
decode runs off the socket thread; no expensive AI on transport threads
the Cognitive Core never crashes due to transport failure (decoupled + event-driven)
existing Flask+SocketIO receiver preserved (legacy 'frame' protocol still works)
